name: ai.fontier/fontier
title: Fontier
description: Every open-licence font family, each with a sourced yes or no for commercial, web and app use.

tools.name: search_fonts
tools.description: Use this to find fonts for a project: by mood or use ("warm editorial serif", "code", "geometric branding"), category, or licence. uses keeps only fonts whose answer is a plain yes for every use listed, e.g. ["commercial","web","app"]. For "which font loads fastest" pass sort "size" (lightest first by the WOFF2 bytes a phone downloads for Latin Regular and Bold from the font's own CDN) and text_only true (sans, serif or mono text faces, no themed or script faces). Every word must match; when no font matches them all, the fonts matching the most words come back and match.all is false with a note. Returns short rows with each use answer, bytes (phone and windows, regular and regularBold) and a url.

query.description: Free text: a family, mood, tag or use. Empty lists everything.

category.description: sans, serif, mono, display, handwriting, icons.

uses.description: Uses that must be a plain yes: commercial, web, app, platform, modify.

offset.description: Skip this many results, to page.

sort.description: relevance (default) or size: lightest first by phone bytes for Regular and Bold.

text_only.description: Only fonts that work as a site's text font: sans, serif or mono, Latin-1 letters, Google's text style tags.

tools.name: get_font
tools.description: Use this for everything about one font: foundry, designers, live version and weights, the CSS URL to load it, facts measured from the font file (cap height, x-height, average width and stem in em, glyph count, scripts, languages, OS/2 embedding bits, WOFF2 bytes per weight, webBytes: what its own CDN sends an iPhone and Windows Chrome for Latin Regular and Regular plus Bold, and fallback @font-face overrides that stop layout shift), the licence ruling for every use with the source and a verbatim quote, how many Y Combinator startup home pages load it (startups), and for hand-reviewed fonts an assessment, tags and pairings.

font.description: Slug or family name, e.g. "satoshi" or "EB Garamond".

tools.name: check_font_license
tools.description: Use this when someone asks "can I use <font> for <use>". Answers yes, no, conditional or unknown, with why, a verbatim quote from the licence, the source URL, a sha256 of the licence text checked and the date checked. Uses: commercial (Use it in commercial work: brand, marketing, products you sell.); web (Serve it on your own website with @font-face, self-hosted or from a CDN.); app (Bundle it inside your own mobile or desktop app.); platform (Offer it to your users as a font they can pick in your product (site builders, design tools, templates).); modify (Change the files: subset, convert formats, edit glyphs.). Omit use to get all of them.

tools.name: pair_fonts
tools.description: Use this when someone asks what font goes with a font ("what pairs with Avenir", "a body font for Montserrat"). Returns the fonts that real websites load with it, counted on a crawl of the home pages of the top sites in one pinned Tranco list: sites loading both, share, lift over chance, example domains, each open partner's licence answers, and the size that lines up both x-heights when both fonts are measured. Works for commercial fonts too (Avenir, Proxima Nova).

font.description: Slug or family name, e.g. "avenir-next" or "Montserrat".
